A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of in-context learning dynamics in linear attention. Their main text, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of loss trajectories, attention-weight dynamics, rank effects, and interactions between in-context and in-weight learning, including Figures 1, 3–5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations and adds experiments involving softmax attention, initialization scales, varying context lengths, higher dimensions, and repeated covariance eigenvalues.

M1.justification: The core ATTNM and ATTNS formulations remain unchanged. v2 adds softmax counterparts in Section 7 and a next-token objective averaging losses across context prefixes in Appendix A.1, Eq. (23). These extend the architectures and training objectives studied without replacing the main linear-attention procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix A.1 extends the fixed-context, final-query scenario to next-token prediction across context lengths 1–31. The synthetic Gaussian linear-regression task family and fixed-task mixtures supporting in-weight learning remain; no new application domain is introduced.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same comparison between merged-key/query attention and its equivalent two-layer MLP. The added experiments study softmax counterparts and variations of the existing model families, without changing comparator membership in the retained comparisons. Newly cited MLP studies are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces prefix-averaged next-token loss, initialization sweeps, higher-dimensional experiments with D=32 or 64 and N=127, and repeated-eigenvalue conditions. Several retained figure captions also change N=32 to 31, while Figure 3 changes H=5 to 4. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether those existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of when the characteristic training dynamics persist: softmax activation in Figure 5, initialization sensitivity in Figure 6, varying contexts and higher dimensions in Appendix A, and repeated eigenvalues in Appendix F.5. v1's rank, weight-alignment, and mixed-task analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions display trajectories from six random initializations in Figures 3 and 4. v2 applies the same practice to its softmax experiment. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, significance tests, or increased run count for retained experiments is reported.

E6.justification: New results show single versus multiple loss drops in softmax attention, shorter plateaus with larger initialization, agreement with revised plateau predictions under next-token loss, and trajectories for higher-dimensional and repeated-eigenvalue settings (Figures 5–8 and 13). The main linear-attention findings and mixed-task results remain, with v1 Figure 10 corresponding to v2 Figure 14.

T1.justification: Appendices A.1 and C.1 generalize covariance, fixed-point, and loss expressions to varying context lengths through E(1/N). v2 also corrects the inverse expression in the global-minimum derivation (v1 C.4; v2 D.4) and revises the minimum-norm proof (v1 D.7; v2 E.7). The principal fixed-point and training-dynamics theory remains.

C1.justification: The claims about two versus exponentially many fixed points, abrupt versus staged learning, and progressive principal-component regression are retained. v2 adds an explicit introduction contribution claiming empirical evidence for corresponding single and multiple loss drops in softmax attention.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds qualified applicability to softmax attention and interprets initialization-dependent dynamics through rich versus lazy learning. Appendix F.5 explains how random initialization can produce plateaus even with repeated eigenvalues, while some seeds skip them. These refine the applicability and mechanism discussion without replacing the central interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Reproducibility section identifying a GitHub repository for reproducing the main results, absent from v1. Initialization specifications are retained from v1 Appendix B.2 in v2 Appendix C.2; no substantial new hardware or runtime documentation appears.

R1.justification: v2 Appendix B adds positioning relative to concurrent and subsequent softmax-dynamics studies by Geshkovski et al. and He et al., and connects the existing MLP equivalence to work on ICL without attention. Some citations, including Henry et al. and Lampinen et al., are removed. The principal positioning against earlier convergence analyses remains.

P1.justification: v2 adopts the ICL abbreviation, condenses explanations and related work, and revises discussion organization. The parallel-head conservation law moves from Section 3.5 to Appendix D.7, and much of the in-weight-learning discussion moves to Appendix G. The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column conference layout, with figures resized and reflowed. v2 adds Figures 5–8 and 13 and removes v1's main-text mixed-task overview, while retaining its underlying results in the appendix. Existing appendix figures are renumbered and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The added softmax, initialization, and context-length experiments provide useful evidence about when v1's dynamics apply, and the code-access statement improves reproducibility documentation. The main theoretical contribution remains intact. These gains are qualified by localized defects in the added mathematics: Eq. (24) omits the context sum, and Eq. (30) introduces extra counting factors in its covariance expansion.
